report.source_text: The differential for this urticarial rash on presentation included a hypersensitivity reaction to environmental toxin, drug reaction, a viral infectious process and autoimmune vasculitis. A detailed history obtained did not reveal any concern for new medication use or change in environmental exposure including linen/soap. Given the progressive worsening over 3 days’ duration, it was likely felt that this was not an anaphylactic reaction. Given the urticarial appearance of the rash, autoimmune vasculitis was felt to be less likely. Consideration of skin biopsy was done, but given a diagnosis of COVID-19, it was felt that a trial of observation with antihistamines could be done initially for the first 24–48 hours, and if no improvement, then to pursue skin biopsy.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Severe urticarial rash as the initial symptom of COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities (obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, atrial fibrillation on warfarin, pulmonary hypertension, and chronic kidney disease stage IV) presented to the emergency department with a 3-day progressive diffuse urticarial rash characterized by erythematous, raised, pruritic wheals on bilateral upper and lower extremities and trunk, sparing palms, soles, and mucosal surfaces. On the third day of the rash, she developed acute shortness of breath with hypoxia (SpO2 84% on room air), requiring supplemental oxygen. COVID-19 PCR testing returned positive. Chest X-ray revealed left basal atelectasis without major infiltrates. The clinical differential diagnosis included hypersensitivity reaction, drug reaction, viral infection, and autoimmune vasculitis, but given the COVID-19 diagnosis, the urticarial rash was attributed to COVID-19 infection. Treatment was initiated with loratadine 10 mg daily, topical triamcinolone 0.1% cream for pruritus management, and remdesivir 200 mg intravenously on day 1 followed by 100 mg intravenously daily for four additional days for COVID-19 pneumonia. The urticarial rash completely resolved within 48 hours of treatment initiation.
